### Describe the bug

With cython 3.3.0, pyx files fails to compile if using the Python `str` type in a comparison with a bytestring. Similar code works for the longest time since 0.29.XX days. Can confirm it compiles if cythonized with cython 3.2.9.


Chuggs with the following error, which makes me think the new comparison code introduced in cython 3.3.0 is not treating byte strings correctly. This only addresses the compilation error. Not sure if the comparison is even valid after the compilation because I can't test it.
```
  File "/Users/User/miniconda3/envs/westpa-2022.15/lib/python3.13/site-packages/Cython/Compiler/ExprNodes.py", line 14444, in find_special_bool_compare_function
    character = ord(self.operand2.value[0])
TypeError: ord() expected string of length 1, but int found
```

```
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^

Cython.Compiler.Errors.CompileError: /Users/User/Documents/Important/Pitt/git/westpa-2022.15/_test.pyx
```

</details>


### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

in _test.pyx:
```cython
cdef:
     str _a

_a = 'a' 

if _a == b'a':
    pass
```

Run:
```
cythonize _test.pyx
```

### Expected behaviour

Cythonization without fail, like in cython <=3.2.9

Note that if the comparison is with `'a'` and not `b'a'`, it compiles fine. Same with setting `_a` to `bytes` or `int`



### OS

Linux, MacOS

### Python version

3.10 ~ 3.14

### Cython version

3.3.0

### Additional context

https://github.com/westpa/westpa/actions/runs/32744608514/job/97487263287

All our (`westpa`'s) latest builds are failing with the same error so... I'm pretty sure it's universal.

EDIT: Updated with a more concise example.

comment_data.body: It definitely shouldn't crash - thanks for the report. It hasn't been a meaningful comparison since Python 2 era though so it should just compile to `if False:`

title: [BUG] 3.3.0 Regression: Python String type comparisons with bytestrings fail during cythonization
